title: A timeline moves, scales and fades a group, panel, stack or grid as one
body:
A canvas `timeline` (acre-5ca447) changes named nodes. `timeline::target` in `crates/acre/src/scene/timeline.rs` rejects a name that belongs to a `group`, `panel`, `stack` or `grid`, with "a timeline changes the nodes inside it". These four kinds already take a name, as in `panel p { ... }`, but lower to no object of their own. `scene::build` opens them and pushes the objects of their children, so a panel's frame and heading are objects whose `source` is the panel's span.

## Proposal

Jack decided the behaviour.

- `fade`, `show`, `hide`, `move` and `scale` name a group, panel, stack or grid and change it as one unit, with everything inside it.
- Opacity multiplies down the tree, so a child's own fade still works inside a faded panel.
- Move offsets every descendant. Scale scales the whole target about the point of its box that `anchor` names, center by default, and not each child about its own center. The four kinds take `anchor` as other nodes do.
- `fill`, `stroke` and `text-color` on one of these kinds is an error that names the target, since it has no single color.
- Connectors and braces attached to nodes inside a moved or scaled group follow them. A connector inside the group whose ends follow nodes is not moved a second time.
- Nested animation composes, so a box inside a moving panel can also move on its own.

Each object carries the motion of every animated group around it, innermost first. The motion an object is drawn with, and the motion a connector reads from it, is its own composed with those.
